label: F-bcda6f

findings.note: PanelService.cs:110 passes `launcher`, which is the constructor's own IProcessLauncher parameter (PanelService.cs:65, also stored at :77), so NoLauncher is never used on the server path.

QuotaCooldowns.cs WriteLocked compares the pruned `next` with the raw `read` on purpose: if any expired entry exists the lists differ and the pruned set is written, and if none exists a no-op change correctly skips the write; callers never send an empty change list (AfterRoundAsync calls Apply only when changes.Count > 0).

QuotaCooldowns.Round.cs DecisionAsync falls through to LiftOf whenever ParkAsync returns null (a transient or undecided refusal that is not parked), and a park beats a sibling Ok only when the refusal qualifies, which is the plan's D5 rule ('a spent refusal wins over a sibling Ok in either order').

Plan D6 requires the probe to reuse the refused launch's working directory, which is AntigravityReadOnly.Home() and not the reviewed repository, so AgyQuotaProbe.cs ReadAsync's `invocation.Request with {...}` is exactly what the plan specifies.

The plan's review record (§11, codex F0) explicitly rejected enforcing the 16 KiB cap, because eviction could un-park a spent row; the budget is one entry per key, a 400-character note cap and expiry pruning on every write, and QuotaCooldowns.cs does all three.
AgyError.cs Parse splits with StringSplitOptions.TrimEntries, which strips the trailing '\r', and JsonDocument.Parse also accepts trailing whitespace, so CRLF input parses correctly.
Plan D4 says 'read on every CanRun, no cache (it is under 16 KiB for ever)', and QuotaCooldowns.Standing re-reads the file by design (the class doc says 'read on every decision with no cache').

Plan D6/§8 sets the probe bound to Timeout = 30 s, enforced by the launcher's tree-killing timeout (AgyQuotaProbe.Bound), and runs it after the round by decision; asking for 10 s or a detached probe contradicts the plan.

AgyQuotaReport.cs Documents tries line-by-line parsing only when the whole stdout fails to parse, and it runs on one small /quota answer per spent key per round, so the cost of the exceptions is negligible and this is a matter of taste.
This repeats index 4: the plan's §11 codex F0 rejected a size cap ('A cap with eviction could un-park a really spent row'), and keys exist only for configured rows until their reset.

QuotaCooldowns.Round.cs DecidedAsync does await the per-key probes one after another, so three spent agy keys that all time out could add about 90 s; the plan only fixes one probe per key at 30 s, but the scenario is rare and the plan accepts post-round waits ('a round takes minutes').

summary: Almost every finding misreads the code at f8a595ab or asks for something the plan explicitly decided against: a cache, a 16 KiB cap, a different working directory, a shorter probe bound. The only usable point is that the per-key probes run one after another, which is a minor latency observation, so a team would gain very little from acting on this review.
